title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and Q4 2026 retrospective
author: Priya Khandelwal
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates the platform systems & services guidance for Q4 2026. It is the canonical runbook and operational playbook for on-call and platform engineers, and includes: the current dashboard set, alert thresholds, runbooks for common incidents, a short how-to checklist for operational tasks, the next-quarter roadmap, and a retrospective covering major incidents and follow-ups from Oct–Dec 2026.

Scope & ownership:
- Scope: core platform services that support Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated control planes, internal platform tooling, and observability pipelines. This includes gateway-api, request-router, model-orchestrator, kv-cache, worker-gpu-pool, metrics-ingest, and platform-console.
- Primary owners:
  - gateway-api: owner SRE (oncall: sres-gateway)
  - request-router: owner serving-runtime team (oncall: serving-runtime)
  - model-orchestrator: owner infra-platform (oncall: infra-platform)
  - kv-cache: owner serving-runtime (oncall: serving-runtime)
  - worker-gpu-pool: owner gpu-fleet (oncall: gpu-fleet)
  - metrics-ingest / observability pipeline: owner eng-platform (oncall: eng-platform)
  - platform-console: owner eng-platform-product (oncall: eng-platform)

System overview (short):
- The platform consists of a public entry (gateway-api -> request-router), model orchestration and scheduling (model-orchestrator), execution pools (worker-gpu-pool, cpu-executors), and a caching layer (kv-cache) that provides prefix/KV cache for inference state. Observability is handled by metrics-ingest -> Datadog/Prometheus + long-term logs to S3/ClickHouse for audits.
- Network segmentation: control plane (internal VPC) and data plane (customer VPCs / dedicated clusters). See reference architecture page for diagrams.

Dashboards & alerts (must be kept in sync):
- Dashboards (primary):
  1) Platform Overview (dashboards/platform/overview): qps, lat50/95/99, downstream error rate, avg GPU utilization, queue depth.
  2) Request Router — performance (dashboards/platform/router-perf): request latency histogram, time-in-queue, rejection rate.
  3) GPU Pool — capacity (dashboards/hardware/gpu-pool): node counts by type, OOMs, preemption events, worker restarts, utilization heatmap per-availability-zone.
  4) Observability pipeline health (dashboards/observability/pipeline): metrics ingest lag, dropped metrics, logs backfill lag, ClickHouse queue.

- Alerting guidelines (global):
  - Pager alerts: page the oncall if user-facing SLOs are violated or if control-plane availability is impacted.
  - Slack alerts: non-urgent thresholds and paging suppression windows go to #platform-ops.
  - Escalation: oncall (15m), senior oncall (30m), engineering manager (60m).

- Key alerts (examples with thresholds):
  1) API error-rate high (pager): 5m rolling error rate > 3% for 2 consecutive windows AND 90th latency > 2s. Runbook: section "API latency & error spike".
  2) Router queue depth (pager): avg queue depth > 5000 requests for 5m or time-in-queue > 200ms p95. Runbook: "Router queue runaway".
  3) GPU node OOM rate (pager): >3 OOMs across cluster in 10m OR worker crash-looping >3 restarts in 15m. Runbook: "GPU node OOM / worker instability".
  4) Metrics ingest lag (page + slack): ingest lag > 10m OR >1% dropped metrics in last 5m. Runbook: "Observability pipeline lag".

Runbooks (concise step-by-step):
- API latency & error spike (oncall):
  1) Verify alert: open Platform Overview dashboard, confirm increased error rate and latency. Note exact time window and affected routes.
  2) Check gateway-api logs for 5xx patterns and request traces (trace id examples).
  3) If 5xx are due to downstream model-orchestrator timeouts: scale model-orchestrator replicas by +2 and unfreeze rollout if canary is misbehaving. Command: kubectl scale deployment/model-orchestrator --replicas=<current+2> -n prod.
  4) If 5xx are external (backend GPU errors), page gpu-fleet and follow GPU runbook.
  5) Post-incident: add an alert suppression window and create JIRA ticket with traces.

- Router queue runaway:
  1) Confirm backlog by querying router metrics (promql: sum(requests_in_queue) by (route)).
  2) Identify backlog root cause: slow downstream, traffic spike, or rate-limit misconfiguration.
  3) If downstream slow: enable emergency fallback to cached-model-variant (config in request-router feature flags) and scale request-router replicas.
  4) If rate limit misconfigured: rollback last rate-limit change and run canary in staging.
  5) Restore normal traffic with controlled release and observe for 45m.

- GPU node OOM / worker instability:
  1) Check node metrics and last OOM logs (kubectl describe node / journalctl).
  2) Isolate affected model shards and migrate live work using eviction-ttl pipeline.
  3) If OOMs persist after migration: upgrade instance type or apply memory-bump configuration on job spec (gpu-worker-memory: +20%).
  4) Rebuild and redeploy suspect worker container with updated quantization flags if memory regressions are suspected.
  5) Re-run perf-test on canary with synthetic load (scripts/test/gpu-smoke.sh).

How-tos (operational checklists):
- Onboard a new service to dashboards & alerts:
  1) Create a new dashboard tile in "Platform Overview" and add to team dashboard list.
  2) Add Prometheus metrics prefix and a dedicated metrics category.
  3) Create two alerts: a pageable SLO violation, and a slack-only operational threshold.
  4) Add runbook link and owner in the dashboard description.

- Deploying a runtime change to request-router (canary flow):
  1) Build image and push to registry (tag: release/<semver>).
  2) Deploy canary (kubectl apply -f k8s/request-router-canary.yaml).
  3) Monitor router-perf for 30 minutes.
  4) If stable, promote to 20% traffic for 1h, then full rollout in 3 steps (20/60/100).
  5) If error rates increase >1% absolute or latency p95 regresses >200ms, rollback immediately.

Operational metrics & SLOs (current):
- SLOs (customer-facing):
  - Control-plane availability: 99.95% monthly (measurement: gateway-api health-checks).
  - API latency: p95 < 1.5s for text-generation endpoints (global).
  - Error rate: <= 0.5% 5xx for production traffic.
- Internal metrics:
  - GPU pool health: node ready% > 99.0
  - Observability ingest lag: <= 2m for Prometheus metrics

(Raw table)
Metric | Target | Measurement
------ | ------ | -----------
Control-plane availability | 99.95% | synthetic healthcheck every 30s
API latency (p95) | <1.5s | production traffic (rolling 30d)
API 5xx error rate | <0.5% | 5m rolling window
GPU node ready | >99.0% | cluster-scrape daily
Observability ingest lag | <2m | last-5m median

Roadmap (next milestones — Q1 2027 focus):
- Short-term (next 90 days):
  - Replace the current router rate-limiter with a token-bucket implementation to reduce head-of-line blocking (owner: serving-runtime).
  - Incremental rollout of region-aware smart routing (owner: infra-platform).
  - Observability pipeline: reduce ingest lag to <60s under 2x traffic (owner: eng-platform).
- Medium-term (Q1–Q2 2027):
  - Autoscaling improvements for GPU pool to reduce cold-start latency for burst workloads.
  - Integration of quality-monitoring traces into the Platform Overview dashboard (owner: applied-ml-and-evals).

Q4 2026 retrospective (high level):
- Major incidents:
  1) 2026-10-21 — Gateway API degraded for 45 minutes due to a canary rollout with an unexpected header handling regression. Root cause: router middleware mis-handling empty X-Client headers. Action: add stricter validation in middleware and improve canary monitoring.
  2) 2026-11-03 — GPU worker pool instability (OOM regressions) during a large model onboarding. Root cause: model binary increased peak memory usage by ~18% vs baseline. Action: introduce a mandatory perf-profile step in model onboarding; block onboarding if memory delta > 12%.
  3) 2026-12-07 — Observability ingest lag spike caused dashboards to show stale data for ~2 hours. Root cause: backfill job misconfiguration and ClickHouse ingestion window saturation. Action: increase ClickHouse consumer concurrency and add backpressure metrics to metrics-ingest.

- What worked:
  - Canary gating policy: in 6/7 rollouts it prevented widespread customer impact.
  - Team communication: dedicated incident channel and runbook checklists reduced mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by 18%.

- Action items (owner / ETA):
  - Add automated perf-profile gate to model onboarding (owner: applied-ml-and-evals, ETA: 2027-01-31).
  - Expand observability pipeline capacity and add tighter throttling (owner: eng-platform, ETA: 2027-02-15).
  - Harden request-router header parsing and add unit & integration tests (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 2026-11-30 — completed).
  - Create a post-incident dashboard template for faster triage (owner: eng-platform, ETA: 2027-01-15).

Reference & links:
- Architecture: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-and-services-reference-architecture
- Model onboarding perf gate: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
- Observability runbooks and dashboards: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and PromQL (examples)
- PromQL: Router queue sum request_in_queue: sum(rate(router_requests_in_queue[1m]))
- Scale model-orchestrator: kubectl -n prod scale deploy model-orchestrator --replicas=5
- Canary deployment check: kubectl get pods -l app=request-router -n prod -o wide

Note: This document must be reviewed quarterly and after any major platform incident. For changes to alert thresholds or dashboard ownership, update the dashboard metadata and ping the reviewers list above.
